Subject: Action items: ACME inference reliability bake-off & failover test plan

Hi Eli / Priya —

Great to connect earlier. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Call highlights
- Top concern: predictable uptime and graceful degradation under bursts (you mentioned 99.95% target).
- Procurement timeline: aiming to finalize vendor short-list by mid-June.
- Data residency: EU for PII; primary region US for low-latency inference.

Proposed bake-off scope (what Redwood will run / measure)
1) Sustained throughput: 1 hour at target QPS (we discussed 150–250 req/s) — measure p95/p99 latency and token cost.
2) Burst behavior: short bursts (up to ~2k rps for 60s) to surface rate-limiting, degraded responses, and retry behavior.
3) Failover probe: simulate zone-level outage and validate cross-region failover and cold-start latency.
4) Error-budget accounting: show error budget burn for each scenario and produce a simple SLO matrix for your SRE team.

Attachments: bakeoff-plan.pdf (detailed steps) and slo-matrix.csv (initial SLO targets + measurement plan).

Questions / asks for you
- Confirm target sustained QPS to use (150 vs 200 vs 250).
- Any IP ranges we should whitelist for probes, and whether test traffic should originate from EU as well as US.
- Do you want Redwood to run the tests using a short-lived API key, or will Acme run from your side with Redwood observing?

Proposed schedule: Tue May 25 or Wed May 26, 10:00 PT start — we expect ~2–3 hours of test execution plus a short debrief.

I’ll wait for your confirmation and will loop in our security contact if you want a scoped test key.

Thanks,

Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

(415) 555-0132

Thanks Jasmine — good recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Target sustained QPS: let’s use 200 req/s for the baseline test. That maps to our expected peak for the initial rollout.
- For burst tests we want to validate both graceful degradation (500–2k rps) and an absolute hard-limit scenario.
- Failover: yes please run one probe originating from EU (Ireland) to validate EU → US failover latency and data residency behavior.
- On procurement: we need a very rough committed pricing estimate for a Dedicated/reserved tier (monthly) so procurement can model cost — ballpark numbers are fine at this stage.

We prefer Redwood to run the tests (we don’t want to generate test traffic from our infra right now). Please provide a time-limited API key and the IPs for your test runners. Also copy our security contact (sec-ops@acme.com) when you send the key.

If Tue 25th 10:00 PT works, lock it in.

Eli — thanks, confirmed. Notes and test plan refinement below.

High-level execution plan (Redwood runs):
- Prep (T-1 day): create short-lived API key scoped to test endpoints, whitelist runner IPs, enable verbose tracing for the test session.
- Test A: Sustained 200 req/s for 60 minutes. Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (generation and total), per-token cost, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate.
- Test B: Burst sequences: 3 bursts of 60s at 500, 1200, 2000 rps, spaced 5 minutes apart. Observe 429s, queuing, and graceful fallback to cheaper model variants if configured.
- Test C: Failover probe: spin up primary workload in us-west-2, then simulate zone failure (drain a node pool). Expected: cross-region failover to us-east-1 with measured failover time and cold-start latency; repeat with a request originating from eu-west-1 to validate routing/policy behavior.

Success criteria / what we’ll deliver
- A CSV of raw measurements (latency histograms + error types), an SLO table showing expected burn rates, and a short slide deck summarizing findings and recommended config (batching / quantization / routing).
- A short list of mitigations we recommend for your production SLOs (circuit-breaker settings, queue depth, fallback model mapping).

Logistics
- I’ll post the scoped API key as a one-time secret to your security alias (sec-ops@acme.com) and to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3Cacme-bakeoff-plan
- Ben’s recommended schedule: Tue May 25 10:00 PT — execution 10:00–13:00 PT, 30m debrief same day. If you want an earlier dry-run we can do a 30m smoke on Mon 24.

Attachments: slo-comparison.xlsx (initial Redwood vs Hyperscaler SLO delta we’ll validate).

Thanks —
